messages:
maria (PM): hey team — quick design review request. I'm iterating on the model catalog compare flow. Main asks: filter chip wrapping behavior, compare table sticky header + badges density, and version pinning affordance when comparing models. figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123 (screens: compare-v2, filters-overflow)

alex (Design): looked at the file. overall +1 on the reduced row height. two things: 1) perf badges feel visually heavy when there are 3+ — they push row content. 2) filter chips wrapping causes the primary action row to jump.

sam (Frontend): on the chip wrapping — if we allow multi-line chips, table scroll becomes confusing on smaller viewports. prefer single-line with an overflow menu (+1 more). implementation-wise we can do `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` and a `+N` collapsed menu.

jo (A11y): flag: the current collapsed `+N` menu is not keyboard accessible in the mock. ensure it's a button with `aria-expanded` and the menu receives focus. also contrast on the new badge colors is marginal on low-brightness themes.

alex (Design): thanks — option: compact badges (icon + 1 letter) when density is low, full badge only on hover. reduces width. thoughts?

maria (PM): that sounds promising. we need discoverability though — maybe a tooltip on hover and an accessible label `aria-label="Performance: latency 12ms; throughput high"`.

devon (Eng): from infra side: note that we show dynamic perf metrics that update every 30s. if badges collapse on hover, the live-update could shift layout. maybe prefer an overlay panel for details to avoid reflow.

sam (Frontend): overlay panel is doable. implement as a popover anchored to the badge, opens on hover/focus/click. keeps layout stable. sample pattern:```<Popover trigger="button" placement="top"> ... </Popover>```

jo (A11y): ensure popover is dismissible with Escape and traps focus if interactive. non-interactive popovers should not trap focus. also add `role="status"` for live metric updates or use `aria-live="polite"` for the metrics inside the popover so screen readers get the change.

alex (Design): another micro-thing: version pinning UX when comparing — currently the pin icon sits inline with the name and can be missed. suggestion: move pin into the left column as a sticky column, with a hover affordance `Pin to compare` and explicit state `Pinned` when active.

maria (PM): that left-column pin feels clearer for multi-row compares. downside: takes horizontal space. can we collapse the left column into a narrow rail with just icons at small widths?

sam (Frontend): yes, responsive rail: >= 960px show full label + pin; < 960px collapse to icon-only rail with tooltip. CSS: `@media (max-width: 960px) .compare-rail {width: 48px}`. we'll keep the pin button target big enough (44px) per touch guidelines.

jo (A11y): one more a11y nit: if users can re-order compared models (drag handle), we need `aria-grabbed` and keyboard reorder support (move up/down). current mock uses only mouse drag.

maria (PM): good call. add keyboard reorder pattern to the spec. devon — anything backend-wise for re-order persistence?

devon (Eng): we persist compare order in user session + optional account-level saved compares. storing the order is cheap. only concern: sync race if two tabs update same compare; we'll version the compare state and use last-write-wins for now.

alex (Design): returning to badges — propose three density states: full (icon + label), compact (icon + tooltip), minimal (dot with tooltip). we can surface density toggle in the compare top bar with a little droplet icon.

sam (Frontend): implementing density toggle is fine. default should be compact. also add `data-testid` on badge elements for e2e tests.

maria (PM): action items: 1) alex update figma with compact/minimal badge options and left-rail pin mock (due EOD). 2) sam & jo to draft accessibility + keyboard spec for chip overflow, popovers, and re-ordering (due tomorrow). 3) devon to confirm persistence approach (end of week). 4) I'll schedule a quick sync Fri 11am PT.

alex (Design): I'll add microcopy too — pin tooltip: `Pin model for compare` / `Unpin model`. badge tooltip: `Latency: 12ms · Throughput: 1.2k/s`.

maria (PM): perfect. small test: sam can you attach a quick prototype link when you have the popover pattern? we'll run it in the sync.

sam (Frontend): will do. prototype by Thurs afternoon.

design-bot: Note: new comment added on figma by alex (Design) — "compact badges + pin rail"

jo (A11y): thanks all — also happy to run a 20min screen-reader check on the prototype before Friday.

maria (PM): amazing, thanks team :thumbsup:
